Author: Scholz et al. ( 107 )
Research question(s)/ hypothesis: Effects of R-af on gross motor functions on participants affected from stroke (right hemiparesis).
Research design: Patients moved their arms in a 3D R-af space, for 9 days of training with R-af (30 min/day)
Auditory stimuli characteristics: X axis: Brightness mapped, increased from left to right Y axis: Pitch mapped, increased from bottom to up Z axis: Volume, increased when closed to the participant
Conclusion: Exp: Enhancements were observed for participants in FMA, ARAT, 9-HPT, and SIS Ct: No enhancements were observed for, but minimally for one participants in FMA, and the other in SIS

Author: Scholz et al. ( 60 )
Research question(s)/ hypothesis: Effects of R-af on gross motor functions on participants affected from stroke (right hemiparesis).
Research design: Patients moved their arms in a 3D sonification space, for 10 days of sonification training (30 min/day).
Auditory stimuli characteristics: X axis: Brightness mapped, increased from left to right Y axis: Pitch mapped, increased from bottom to up Z axis: Volume, increased when closed to the participant
Conclusion: Exp: Significant enhancements were observed for participants in movement smoothness, FMA, SIS as compared to Ct Enhancements were observed in ARAT, BBT and 9-HPT Ct: No significant enhancements were observed post sham training

Author: Kim et al. ( 112 )
Research question(s)/ hypothesis: Effects of RAC on arm reaching performance in patients affected from stroke
Assessment tools: Movement time, movement unit, elbow extension range of motion by 3D motion detection, triceps, biceps brachii muscle activation and co-contraction ratio from EMG
Research design: Repetitive reaching task performed with/without RAC from affected arm
Auditory stimuli characteristics: RAC at patients preferred pace of movement
Conclusion: Significant enhancement in elbow range of motion, tricpes brachii activation with RAC Significant reduction in co-contraction ratio, movement time and movement unit with RAC

Author: Shahine and Shafshak ( 113 )
Research question(s)/ hypothesis: Effect of RAC on arm function in patients affected from stroke
Assessment tools: FMA and transcutaneous magnetic stimulation eliciting motor evoked potential in paretic abductor pollicis brevis (motor evoked potential resting threshold, central motor conduction time)
Research design: Pre-test, BATRAC for 1-h session/day, 3seesions/week, for 8 weeks, post-test
Auditory stimuli characteristics: RAC at patients preferred pace of movement (frequency 0.25–1/s)
Conclusion: Significant enhancement in FMA, motor evoked potential amplitude ratio after BATRAC Significant reduction in motor evoked potential resting threshold, central motor conduction time after bilateral arm training with RAC, and in Exp as compared to Ct

Author: Whitall et al. ( 115 )
Research question(s)/ hypothesis: Effect of RAC in arm reaching patients affected from stroke
Assessment tools: FMA, wolf motor test (time, weight, function, SIS (emotion, hand, strength), isokinetic strength (elbow flexion-extension nonparetic side, elbow extension paretic side) and isometric strength (shoulder extension, wrist flexion-extension nonparetic side, shoulder extension, wrist extension, elbow flexion paretic side)
Research design: Pre-test, BATRAC for 1-h session, 3 times/week for 6 weeks, post-test
Auditory stimuli characteristics: RAC at patients preferred pace of movement
Conclusion: Significant enhancement in FMA, wolf motor test (weight, function), SIS (hand, strength), isokinetic strength (elbow extension nonparetic side, elbow extension paretic side), isometric strength (shoulder extension, wrist extension nonparetic side, shoulder extension) assessment in Exp after training with RAC Significant reduction in wolf motor test (time) in Exp after training with RAC Significant enhancement in isokinetic strength (elbow flexion nonparetic side), isometric strength (wrist flexion, nonparetic side, wrist extension paretic side) in Exp as compared to Ct

Author: Secoli et al. ( 117 )
Research question(s)/ hypothesis: Effect of RAC on tracking task in patients affected from stroke.
Sample description, age: (M ± S.D): Exp: (affect left hemisphere) 8F, 6M (56.3 ± 12.3) Ct: (affect right hemisphere) 1F, 4M (61.8 ± 5) Healthy: 2F, 12M (27 ± 7.5)
Assessment tools: Arm movements with robot assisted force production to execute task in Z dimension Positioning error in Z dimension
Research design: Patients performed tracking task with robot assisted device in with/without visual distractor task and/or with/without RAC
Auditory stimuli characteristics: Tonal beeps sampled at frequency of 800 Hz and lasting for 0.1 s Frequency manipulated proportionally to vector magnitude of position tracking error within dead-zone. Error direction determined by left and right channel of auditory input
Conclusion: Significant reduction in robot assisted force in Exp when auditory input was delivered, suggesting significant enhancement in arm functioning Significant reduction in robot assisted force for the paretic side as compared to healthy side with RAC No effect on position tracking accuracy
